q: Match: (A) Art 14 (B) Art 15 (C) Art 16 (D) Art 17 with 1-no discrimination on 5 grounds, 2-equality before law, 3-untouchability abolished, 4-equality of opportunity in public employment.
expl: UPSC 2004 pattern. 14=equality before law, 15=5 grounds, 16=opportunity, 17=untouchability.

q: Consider: (a) Art 15(4) is an exception to 15(1). (b) Art 16(4) flows from 16(1) as real equality. (c) Art 14 bans all classification. Correct?
expl: Indra Sawhney 1992: 15(4)/16(4) emphatic statement, not exception. Art 14 allows reasonable classification.

q: Untouchability protection (Art 17) falls under which Right?
expl: UPSC 2020. Art 14-18 = Right to Equality, Art 17 inside it.

q: Valid classification under Art 14 needs:
expl: Two-test: differentia must exist AND connect to law's object.

q: President/Governor immunity from courts is under:
expl: 361 = immunity exception to Art 14. 359 = emergency suspension. 31C = DPSP shield.

q: Art 15 prohibits discrimination on how many grounds, and which is NOT one?
expl: Exactly 5: religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth. Descent/residence not in Art 15.

q: Residence condition for state public employment can be laid down by:
expl: Art 16: only Parliament prescribes residence requirement.

q: E.P. Royappa (1974) laid down:
expl: Royappa: equality vs arbitrariness sworn enemies; reasonableness is the test. Maneka 1978 followed.

q: Which statement on Art 14 scope is correct?
expl: Art 14: 'any person' - citizens + foreigners. Arts 15-16: citizens only.

q: Accepting a foreign title requires:
expl: Art 18: no titles from state; foreign title only with President consent.

q: A state law bars private homeowners from selling to one community. Challenged under Art 15. Correct outcome?
options: No Art 15 - private home not state resort/shop
expl: Medium trap: 15(2) covers shops/public resorts maintained by state funds, not private homes. Private bias is immoral but not Art 15.

q: Art 15(5) reservation in private unaided colleges EXCEPTS:
expl: 93rd Amendment: 15(5) covers private unaided but expressly excepts minority educational institutions.

q: 44th Amendment 1978 changed emergency ground from 'internal disturbance' to:
expl: 44th fixed 42nd excess: 352 now war/external aggression/armed rebellion only.

q: Assertion (A): Art 16(4) reservation can exceed 50% routinely. Reason (R): Indra Sawhney fixed 50% ceiling with extraordinary exceptions. Correct?
expl: Tough: 50% ceiling is the rule (Balaji/Indra Sawhney); crossing needs extraordinary far-flung-area justification. Routine excess false.

q: Which pair is WRONG?
expl: 91st 2003 = ministers 15% cap. EWS = 103rd 2019 (15(6)/16(6)). Classic number-swap trap.

q: Maneka Gandhi 1978 added to Art 14 doctrine that:
options: Procedure must be fair, just, reasonable - arbitrariness test
expl: Maneka extended Royappa: any procedure under Art 21 must be fair/just/reasonable; arbitrary procedure violates 14+21.

q: Military and academic distinctions under Art 18 are:
expl: Art 18 bans state TITLES; military/academic distinctions expressly permitted.

q: Creamy layer exclusion from reservation flows from:
expl: Mandal judgment: forward among backwards (creamy layer) excluded to keep real equality.

q: Art 31C as narrowed by Minerva Mills 1980 shields:
options: Only laws giving effect to Art 39(b)-(c)
expl: 42nd tried all-DPSP shield; Minerva cut to 39(b)-(c) only. High-frequency trap.

q: Three statements: (a) Art 14 covers companies in some cases (b) Art 15 covers foreigners (c) Art 17 has no exception. Correct set?
expl: a true (juristic person), b false (citizens only), c true (absolute). Medium elimination drill.
